http://www.bgnes.com/politics/european-c.text: The European Commission will examine whether amendments adopted by the Romanian Parliament to the Decarbonisation Law could affect the implementation of Milestone 114 of Romania's National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP), which relates to energy sector reform and the phased closure of coal and lignite-fired power plants, a European Commission spokesperson told AGERPRES in a report by Florin Ștefan and Simona Clodnischi. According to the spokesperson, the Commission is aware of the amendments adopted on 5 August 2026, which make the closure of coal and lignite-fired power plants conditional on the availability of alternative low-carbon generation capacity. It will carefully assess these changes, as they have not yet been promulgated by the Romanian President. The Commission stressed that it would evaluate any potential risk to the fulfilment of Milestone 114 and reiterated that any backtracking on the agreed reforms would be subject to close scrutiny, with possible financial consequences for Romania. Brussels also said it is closely monitoring Romania's electricity security in coordination with the national authorities and the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity (ENTSO-E). At this stage, it sees no immediate cause for concern, as electricity supplies remain stable. The Commission also expressed its readiness to provide support through the available instruments under EU law to address the consequences of the drought and, if necessary, to convene an extraordinary meeting of the Electricity Coordination Group. Regarding the 31 August deadline for the closure of coal-fired power plants, the spokesperson noted that the amendments linking plant closures to the availability of alternative generation capacity could undermine the irreversibility of the process required under Milestone 114. The spokesperson also referred to the separate Milestone 119A, which requires the decommissioning of 710 MW of coal and lignite-fired capacity, while emphasising that the choice of which specific facilities to retire remains Romania's responsibility. Romania's Chamber of Deputies approved the Decarbonisation Law on Wednesday with an amendment proposed by the Social Democratic Party (PSD), stipulating that coal and lignite-fired generating capacity may only be phased out once equivalent new capacity has been built. During the parliamentary debate, National Liberal Party (PNL) spokesperson Ionel Bogdan warned that repeated attempts to amend key legislation could jeopardise Romania's commitments under the NRRP, cautioning that the country risks losing billions of euros in funding as a result of the changes. | BGNES

Artificial intelligence can accelerate claims resolution Events Our Brands Outsourcing Today Automotive Today Sustainability Today Home News Nusco appoints Nello Nusco as Strategy & Investments Director Nusco appoints Nello Nusco as Strategy & Investments Director News Top stories People Real estate Published on September 1, 2026 By Petre Barac Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Email Nusco announces the appointment of Nello Nusco as Strategy & Investments Director. This marks an important milestone in the company’s evolution, with the primary objective of advancing its investment strategy in an increasingly mature real estate market. Nello holds a Master’s degree in Management Engineering with a specialization in Finance from the Polytechnic University of Turin. He has accumulated more than eight years of professional experience in Milan, working with leading consulting firms, where he focused primarily on financial services and asset management. Nello joined the Nusco Group’s Romanian operations and the family’s business in Romania at the beginning of this year. In his new role, he leads the company’s development initiatives, drawing on his expertise in business model optimization, project management, and operational management. “I am honored to join the Nusco team and a family business with such a strong heritage, one that I am incredibly proud to be part of. I am also excited about this new step in my career, in a market with such significant potential as Romania, which has now reached a truly mature stage of development, as demonstrated by Nusco’s ambitious projects currently underway. This is what attracted me most to the role, and I look forward to identifying new investment opportunities and strategic partnerships together with the Nusco team, built on innovation, efficiency, and a long-term vision. I would also like to thank Michele Nusco and the entire Nusco team for the trust they have placed in me,” said Nello Nusco. As Strategy & Investments Director, he is responsible for identifying new growth opportunities, developing and implementing sustainable business models, and expanding Nusco’s portfolio through strategic initiatives and value-added investments. “In an increasingly globalized economy and a progressively more mature real estate market, Nello and his international expertise join the company at a stage of development focused on delivering mixed-use projects that support a more flexible lifestyle. The expansion of our management team comes at a particularly dynamic phase of our business and reflects our steady growth, following the signing of partnerships with Hyatt, Medicana, and Little London – facilities that will be integrated into Nusco City,” stated Michele Nusco, CEO of Nusco. As the development of Nusco City – one of Bucharest’s largest urban regeneration projects – continues, the company is currently advancing Phase III while preparing the concept for the next phase. At the same time, Nusco is expanding its development capabilities beyond residential real estate through the construction of dedicated buildings that will house the Hyatt Dual Brand hotel, the Medicana hospital, and the Little London educational facility.
